transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-20 15:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Sophie Martinez (Redwood AE), Derek Wu (Redwood SE), Ami Patel (Meteor Tech - Head of AI), Jordan Kim (Platform), Ravi Singh (Security), unknown participant joined as Speaker 2

Summary: quick product walkthrough of JSON mode + runtime orchestration. Focus on how to enforce typed outputs, route tool calls to internal services, and maintain guardrails for safety + data controls.

Topics covered (auto-gen): API quickstart, Console demo, Optimize recommendations, schema enforcement, tool calling patterns, fallback orchestration, security (KMS/SSO/SOC2), pilot next steps.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Sophie (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick roll call — I see Ami, Jordan, Ravi, and Derek and I from Redwood. We're planning 45-ish of demo and then 10 for Q&A. Sound good?
[00:08] Ami (Meteor): Yep that's great. We're looking to see how Redwood handles typed outputs and safe tool invocations, especially because we have two internal services that the assistant needs to hit.
[00:17] Derek (Redwood SE): Awesome. We'll show the API flow, the Console view for schema enforcement, and then the Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization. We'll also demo runtime fallbacks so if a model variant is unavailable requests can route to cheaper or regional backends.
[00:29] Jordan (Meteor): Quick context: our stack is GCP, and we have a hybrid infra — some data in us-central but a portion needs to stay in eu-west. We also want SSO via Okta and KMS-controlled keys, plus SOC2 level logs.
[00:42] Sophie: Perfect, we'll call out the SSO and KMS bits as we go. Derek, can you kick us off with the JSON mode walkthrough?
[00:48] Derek: Sure. So JSON mode is an opinionated runtime where outputs are validated against a schema before being surfaced. I'll share my screen — let me know if the screen shares come through.
[00:55] [screen share noise] Speaker 2: (inaudible)
[01:05] Derek: Okay, on screen now — Console -> Model -> "Aurora-typed"... sorry, internal name. First thing: you can attach a JSON Schema to a route or to the prompt template. When the model outputs, the runtime attempts to parse and validate. If it fails, we have three configurable policies: reject, attempt-correct (repair via another model call), or fallback to a structured extraction pipeline.
[01:30] Ami: When you say repair, is that an auto-call back to the same model or a different step?
[01:35] Derek: Good question. Repair is an internal micro-call that can use a smaller, cheaper model or the same variant depending on policy. You can also pass in contextual constraints — think of it as a rewrite pass trying to coerce output to the schema.
[01:47] Jordan: We care about determinism. If you repair, do you log the intermediate outputs and the reason?
[01:52] Derek: Yes — every repair attempt is logged in the Console trace. You get token-level diffs and a trace ID you can push into your observability pipeline.
[02:00] Ravi: Security — are those intermediate logs stored in plaintext? We need encryption at rest and strict access control.
[02:06] Sophie: All logs can be configured with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for encryption at rest, and RBAC controls tie into SSO providers. By default hosted has short retention, but for Dedicated/Private you can set retention and export flows.
[02:18] Jordan: Sounds good. Can you show tool calling with schemas? We have an internal ticket service and a secure shipping API we want reachable but locked down.
[02:25] Derek: Yep, switching to the API example. So the model can emit a JSON with a field "tool_call" where the schema defines allowed tool names and parameters. The runtime validates the schema and then consults routing policies — e.g., only calls to "internal-ticket-v1" are allowed from our VPC-subnet, and we can whitelist specific endpoints.
[02:44] Ami: What about secrets — like API keys for those services?
[02:47] Derek: We provide a secrets vault integration that injects ephemeral credentials at call-time; keys are never surfaced to the model. For Private deployments you can integrate to your KMS directly so we never handle raw credentials.
[02:58] [00:03 of second block - slight overlap/interruption] Speaker 2: how about latency while waiting for external API?
[03:05] Derek: We have async tool calling patterns — the runtime can stream a provisional response to the user while an async job completes, or you can block and wait. For blocking calls we surface a streaming progress token so the client UI can animate progress.
[03:18] Jordan: If the external service fails, can you do automatic retries or fallbacks?
[03:22] Derek: Yes. Retry policies are pluggable — exponential backoff, circuit breaker, or fallback to a cached response. We also support a policy to route to a secondary tool implementation (e.g., a cheaper region).
[03:33] Ami: Okay, show us a concrete prompt + schema example.
[03:36] Derek: On the Console snippet — prompt plus schema: the model is asked to return an object {"intent":"string","entities":[{"type":"string","value":"string"}],"tool_call":{"name":"string","args":{}}}. When the model returns, the runtime applies AJV-like validation and then either executes the tool or raises a structured error.
[03:57] Ami: AJV-like — we use JSON Schema v7 compat, right?
[04:01] Derek: Exactly, v7 compatible. You can also attach custom validators if you need extra business logic.
[04:06] Jordan: One of our requirements is not to leak PII into logs — are there scrubbers?
[04:11] Derek: Yes, we have pattern-based scrubbers and post-processing hooks; you can register a sanitizer function in Private that runs inside your VPC so raw PII never leaves.
[04:20] Ravi: SOC2 is table stakes for us; show me where the audit logs live.
[04:25] Sophie: In Hosted we provide an audit-log export API and long-term storage add-on. For Private, logs can be forwarded to your SIEM — we support Splunk and BigQuery exporters. Everything is tagged with trace IDs and masked if configured.
[04:37] Derek: Now switching to Optimize — quick recommendations: for conversational workloads with many short LLM turns we suggest prefix caching (KV cache hits) and a modest batching window. If you have longer context you might opt for a quantized variant to save cost. The Console's Optimize tab will simulate cost and latency tradeoffs for your route.
[04:59] Jordan: Can Optimize give me actual dollars per 1M tokens with our traffic profile?
[05:03] Derek: Yes, you can upload a sample traffic trace and Optimize will simulate TCO across variants and quantization. It outputs an expected per-token cost and estimated p95 latency.
[05:12] Ami: For the pilot we need a 2-week proof: 500k tokens/day, and we want to validate accuracy on 5 critical prompts. Can you run evals?
[05:20] Derek: Absolutely. We can run batch evals and surface regressions tied to your prompt sets. We'll hook those to alerts in Console so you can see quality drift.
[05:28] Jordan: On networking — can we pin the Dedicated pool to our VPC region? We want lower cross-region egress.
[05:33] Sophie: Dedicated can be reserved in region and pinned; autoscaling works within the pool but we can restrict region and AZ. For strict data residency we recommend Private with the customer-managed control plane.
[05:45] Ravi: If we go Private, what's the install surface and support SLA?
[05:49] Sophie: Private installs are orchestrated via our on-prem bundle. We provide an installation runbook and 12-week onboarding support in Enterprise tier; SLAs available on Dedicated+Enterprise. We can share the runbook as part of next steps.
[06:00] [06:00 timestamp - slight garble] Speaker 2: (murmur)
[06:05] Derek: Quick demo: I'll call the API with a prompt and schema. (Types) POST /v1/generate with JSON schema in the body. Response: streaming tokens that are validated; you get an extra envelope field "_validation" with status ok/repaired/failed and trace_id.
[06:28] Ami: Could that envelope contain sensitive data?
[06:31] Derek: No, envelope is metadata only. If you enable debug traces those are gated behind RBAC and only available to explicit roles.
[06:38] Jordan: Competitors we looked at required us to build our own router for failover; sounds like Redwood has that built in?
[06:45] Sophie: Yes, smart routing is first-class. You define policy rules in Console — route by region, cost tier, or model family. You can set automatic fallback to cheaper quantized variants during spike events.
[06:57] Ravi: How does billing work if we route across variants? We need clear cost attribution per team.
[07:03] Derek: Billing is token-level and route-tagged. Console provides cost granularity per route/model and per API key so teams can be charged back accurately.
[07:12] Ami: Ok that's helpful. Anything about latency SLOs?
[07:16] Sophie: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed throughput and latency tiers. Hosted has p95 targets published per model family; we'll share the published perf matrix in the follow-up.
[07:25] Jordan: One more — for the tool calls we want a manual approval gate for high-risk ops. Is that possible?
[07:31] Derek: Yes — you can configure a policy that marks certain tool calls as "approval_required" which routes the call to an approvals queue and emits a webhook to your ops tool.
[07:39] Ami: Great. Let's talk pilot logistics — timeline would be two weeks to spin up a Dedicated sandbox or Private eval environment?
[07:46] Sophie: We can spin a Dedicated sandbox in a cloud region within 3–5 business days once the contract is signed. Private eval typically takes longer depending on network access — usually 2–4 weeks.
[07:58] Jordan: Budget is conservative, so we'd prefer a Dedicated pilot first and then consider Private if residency concerns still exist.
[08:04] Ravi: I'll run the legal and compliance checklist but we need SOC2 & KMS docs before we go forward.
[08:10] Sophie: Understood — will send security pack and a proposed statement of work.
[08:15] [crosstalk — someone typing]
[08:20] Derek: Final quick note — for schema drift we recommend hooking the evals to a daily job. If a prompt's accuracy falls below threshold the runtime can automatically revert to a golden model version.
[08:32] Ami: Love that. Thanks, that's the kind of guardrail we need.
[08:36] Sophie: Ok, let me recap action items — Sophie will send pricing and security pack; Derek will share the perf template and schedule an hour for benchmarking; Meteor will identify the 5 critical prompts and compliance contact.
[08:50] Jordan: Sounds good. We'll aim to have the prompts and compliance point by Monday.
[08:55] Ravi: I'm adding legal to the thread.
[08:58] Sophie: Great, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the bench next week. Thanks everyone.
[09:03] [meeting ends — recording stops]

Notes about transcription: occasional mislabels (Speaker 2), and brief audio overlaps. Some product names anonymized during recording (internal model names).
